I'll start by reading the test file to see what is expected.

ACTION {"tool": "read_file", "args": {"path": "tests/test_core.py"}}

Now I'll read the core source to see how word_count and top_words are implemented.

ACTION {"tool": "read_file", "args": {"path": "textstats/core.py"}}

I have both core files; the likely issues are the tokenizer regex dropping apostrophes and the sort lacking an alphabetical tiebreak. I'll check `__init__.py` to confirm the exports are fine.

ACTION {"tool": "read_file", "args": {"path": "textstats/__init__.py"}}

Two bugs in textstats/core.py cause the failures; `__init__.py` is fine.

1. In `tokenize`, change `return re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower())` to `return re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text.lower())`. The old regex splits "don't" in two.
2. In `top_words`, change `return sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:n]` to `return sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:n]`. The old key has no alphabetical tiebreak.
